title: S and C Share a Sound
kidRule: When S and C stand together right before E, I or Y, they make just one sound: '/s/'! The C stays quiet and lets the S do the talking, as in SCISSORS, SCENE and SCIENCE.
hint: We hear only '/s/' here, but two letters are writing it. A quiet letter hides right after the S. Which one?
reminder: The '/s/' sound here is spelled S-C, with a quiet C right before E, I or Y.

check.question: Why can't we hear the C in SCISSORS?
check.correctAnswer: When S-C comes right before E, I or Y, the two letters share one '/s/' sound!
distractors: Because C is always quiet at the start of a word
Because the double S in the middle makes the C quiet

words.def: A tool with two blades that open and close for cutting paper, cloth, or hair.
words.sent: I used scissors to cut out a paper star.
words.story: People were already cutting with these in ancient Egypt, more than 3,000 years ago!
words.card: The *scissors* snipped my *so*ck into a tiny hat for the hamster!

words.def: A person who studies the world by watching closely, asking questions, and doing tests.
words.sent: The scientist looked at a drop of pond water under a microscope.
words.story: This word is less than 200 years old! It was made up in the 1830s. Before that, people who studied nature were called natural philosophers.
words.card: The *scientist* and the den*tist* built a toothbrush for a crocodile!

words.def: One part of a play or a movie, or a place where something happens.
words.sent: The first scene of the play takes place in a castle.
words.story: This word comes from the Greek 'skene', the tent or hut behind the stage in ancient Greek theaters where the actors changed their costumes!
words.card: In the last *scene*, a penguin danced in the *cen*ter of the stage!

words.sent: We watched the hot air balloon descend slowly into the field.
words.story: A peregrine falcon can descend faster than any other animal. When it dives, it can go more than 200 miles an hour!
words.card: The stairs *descend* and *end* in a swimming pool full of pudding!

words.def: A curved shape, like the moon when only a thin slice of it is showing.
words.sent: A thin crescent of moon hung over the rooftops.
words.story: The French word for this shape is 'croissant'. That is how the curved, buttery breakfast roll got its name!
words.card: I paid one *cent* for a *crescent* moon made of cheese!

words.def: To interest someone so much that they cannot stop looking or listening.
words.sent: Shiny beetles fascinate my little brother.
words.story: Octopuses fascinate the people who study them. They can solve puzzles and even unscrew the lid of a jar!
words.card: *Cin*namon rolls *fascinate* my dog, and he stares at them for hours!

words.sent: We took the scenic road along the coast.
words.story: The Blue Ridge Parkway is a scenic road that winds through the mountains of Virginia and North Carolina for 469 miles!
words.card: We had a pic*nic* on the *scenic* hilltop with a very polite bear!

words.sent: The hikers began to ascend the steep trail.
words.story: The first people known to ascend to the very top of Mount Everest were Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, in 1953!
words.card: The *as*tronaut waved as her rocket began to *ascend* past a flying sandwich!

words.def: The training that helps you follow rules and keep working, even when it is hard.
words.sent: Learning the violin takes discipline and patience.
words.story: This word comes from the Latin 'discipulus', which means a student or a learner!
words.card: It takes *discipline* to wait in *line* behind forty slow snails!

words.sent: The crossing guard wore a fluorescent yellow vest.
words.story: This word was named after a mineral called fluorite, which can glow in beautiful colors under ultraviolet light!
words.card: My *fluorescent* socks glow in the dark and have the *scent* of pickles!
